Full summary: Filed #41 (v2.1): twining_why is unbounded — full-rationale dumps hit 350KB in a field session, agent skipped reading them, Gate 1 value lost. Diagnosed mechanism and proposed budgeted/ranked/tiered response.
Decisions: Chose to file the twining_why size blowup as a v2.1 issue (#41) with a ranked-tier + token-budget design direction over patching a hard result-size cap — a bare cap would silently drop the most relevant decisions, while ranking + tiering + drill-down preserves Gate 1 value; also over client-side-only mitigation (Claude Code's save-to-disk preview), which already exists and demonstrably loses the signal.
Findings: twining_why has no size discipline: DecisionEngine.why() (src/engine/decisions.ts:327) returns every match with full rationale — no max_tokens budget, no limit, no status filter (superseded included). twining_assemble budgets at ~4000 tokens and defers to why, making why the only unbudgeted decision read path.; getByScope (src/storage/decision-store.ts:70) matches bidirectional prefix on scope AND affected_files — a single-file query pulls in all ancestor-scoped decisions and every decision that ever listed the file, at equal weight. Match set grows monotonically with project age.; Measured on this repo (170 decisions, avg rationale 234 chars): why('src/') → 96 matches ~48KB; field project at ~350KB is the same linear curve further along.; need: v2.1 fix per #41 — relevance ranking (specificity > status > recency), two detail tiers under max_tokens budget, exclude superseded by default, ids drill-down param so truncation never strands information.
